extracted.intended_audience: readers, students, and writers interested in poetry and poetic forms
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the genre and form of the elegy — its typical tone, thematic aim, and a common stanzaic/metered form associated with it (the elegiac stanza). Useful for poets and students learning to identify or compose elegies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegy (genre) — tone and thematic arc
rubrics_metrics.description: In traditional English poetry, an elegy is often a melancholy poem that laments its subject’s death but ends in consolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elegies typically mourn or lament a death (melancholy tone) but conventionally move toward consolation by the close. This is a generic, traditional characterization of the elegy rather than a strict rule; modern elegies may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegiac stanza (form) — stanzaic, rhyme, and meter
rubrics_metrics.description: Elegiac stanza is a quatrain with the rhyme scheme ABAB and written in iambic pentameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The elegiac stanza emerged in the 18th century but its use has not been exclusive to elegies — the stanza form (four lines, ABAB, iambic pentameter) can appear in other contexts as well.
